title: Notice Walk Detective
intro: Look around a Michigan backyard. Tap what you notice, then pick the questions we can test.
note: This is a model of a real notice walk. Go outside or look around your room and notice real things too, then do the paper-towel test from the lesson. Do it with a grown-up.
summary: Noticing and asking are science, and your tally is data — just like the class chart of 4 smooth things and 5 bumpy things. A question we can test changes one thing and measures one thing, like the towel test: Towel A held 5 drops, Towel B held 8 drops.

items.label: Maple leaf
items.say: A maple leaf. It feels smooth.

items.label: Beach glass
items.say: A piece of beach glass from the lake. Smooth!

items.label: Old brick
items.say: An old brick. Rough and bumpy.

choices.label: Which paper towel holds more drops of water?
choices.why: Yes! Change one thing: the towel. Measure one thing: the drops. The lesson did this: Towel A held 5 drops, Towel B held 8 drops.

choices.label: Why is water wet?
choices.why: A test changes one thing and measures one thing. This question has nothing to change or count yet.

choices.label: Is blue the prettiest color?
choices.why: Prettiest is an opinion. A test measures something we can count or compare.

choices.label: Which ball rolls farther: on grass or on the sidewalk?
choices.why: Yes! Change one thing: the ground. Measure one thing: how far the ball rolls.

choices.label: Why is the sky blue?
choices.why: A test changes one thing and measures one thing. We cannot change the sky or count it here yet.

choices.label: What is the best backyard?
choices.why: Best is an opinion. A test measures something we can count or compare.

choices.label: Which soaks up more water: a sponge or a paper towel?
choices.why: Yes! Change one thing: what soaks up the water. Measure one thing: how much water it holds.

choices.label: Why do leaves fall off trees?
choices.why: A test changes one thing and measures one thing. This question has nothing we can change and count yet.

choices.label: Are pine cones nicer than stones?
choices.why: Nicer is an opinion. A test measures something we can count or compare.
